paragraphs: Here's what I want you to carry out of Psalm 64, friend. David doesn't answer the schemers with a scheme of his own. He brings his "voice of complaint" to God and asks Him to "Hide me from the scheming of the wicked" (Psalm 64:1-2). When somebody is sharpening their tongue at you, your first move is to take it to God, not to fire back.

The wicked in this psalm think nobody is watching. They ask, "Who will see them?" and call their plan perfect (Psalm 64:5-6). But then the psalm turns: "But God will shoot them with arrows; suddenly they will be wounded" (Psalm 64:7). I think that's the comfort here, because the One who sees the hidden things doesn't miss a single one of them. Hiding only works on people, never on God.

So where does that leave you? David ends with "Let the righteous rejoice in the LORD and take refuge in Him; let all the upright in heart exult" (Psalm 64:10). He started the psalm afraid and ends it with joy, and the whole way, God was his hiding place. Friend, when the sharp words come, run to Him, and then get ready to exult. I'll be right there hopping on my gold base.
